request.message: Use AWS for this synthetic architecture qualification. Correlate synthetic logs and distributed traces to explain a service incident. Include collection, redaction, storage/search, an AI analysis runtime and an operator-facing answer with source evidence. Treat log text as untrusted. Acceptance criteria: Redact secrets before model input; Link conclusions to exact trace or log IDs; Prompt injection in a log cannot issue tool calls; Missing spans yield uncertainty rather than invented causes; Repeated ingestion preserves a consistent incident timeline. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

response.message:
I've drawn the full AWS pipeline for this qualification, with redaction applied before anything reaches the model. Synthetic services send logs to CloudWatch Logs and traces to X-Ray. A Firehose transform Lambda redacts secrets, then the data goes to an S3 archive and an OpenSearch index. That index uses event-ID document keys, so ingesting the same data again keeps one consistent incident timeline. An operator calls an IAM-protected API, and a Lambda analysis runtime retrieves the evidence and sends it to Bedrock through Bedrock Guardrails. Every conclusion must cite a real trace or log ID, and the model has no tool-calling path.

**First local test:** we'd load a synthetic incident that contains a fake secret, a prompt-injection line and a missing span. With a scripted mock model, that run only shows our own code paths work: redaction, ID-citation checks, ignoring the injected line, flagging uncertainty, and a consistent timeline when ingested twice. It says nothing about how well a real model reasons.

**Real model check:** checking the model's actual behaviour means running the same tests against a Bedrock model. That needs a confirmed region, account access and model entitlement, and none of those are verified yet.

**Built-in support:** apart from the Bedrock connection, the export can't generate any of this pipeline yet. That part needs engineering work, not just a diagram fix.

I've recorded AWS as your cloud and drafted your five acceptance criteria as must-have requirements.

**Question:** which country do these logs and traces have to stay in, so we can choose the AWS region?

proposal.title: AWS log/trace incident analysis – end-to-end draft
proposal.body: Scope: synthetic logs and traces → redaction → archive/search → Lambda analysis with Bedrock behind Guardrails → evidence-cited answer to an IAM-authenticated operator. Assumptions: region not selected; Bedrock model, access and quotas unverified; only the Bedrock binding is typed, so the rest of the pipeline still needs engineering. Nothing has been deployed.

data.label: Synthetic services
data.description: Synthetic workload emitting logs and OpenTelemetry traces (with seeded secrets, injection text and missing spans for testing).

data.label: Log collection
data.description: Receives service logs; a subscription filter forwards them to Firehose.

data.label: Trace collection
data.description: Stores distributed traces; the analysis runtime reads them by trace ID and redacts span metadata before model input.

data.label: Log delivery
data.description: Buffers logs, invokes the redaction transform, delivers to S3 and OpenSearch.

data.label: Secret redaction
data.description: Firehose transform: pattern and entropy redaction of secrets; assigns a deterministic event ID per log line.

data.label: Redacted archive
data.description: Versioned archive of redacted logs, used to replay ingestion.

data.label: Log & timeline search
data.description: Indexes redacted logs using the event ID as the document ID, so re-ingestion updates records instead of duplicating them; searchable by trace ID and time.

data.label: Incident operator
data.description: Existing IAM-authenticated operator; outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Incident query API
data.description: HTTP API with IAM authorization; no anonymous access.

data.label: Incident analysis runtime
data.description: Uses fixed read-only code paths to retrieve evidence (no model-issued tool calls), redacts again, builds a timeline and sends the evidence to the model, labelled as untrusted data. Checks that every cited trace/log ID exists, flags missing spans as uncertainty, and returns an answer with evidence IDs.

data.label: Prompt safety filter
data.description: Applied to the model call: detects prompt attacks and sensitive information (a second layer behind the Lambda redaction).

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: Direct foundation model through the Converse API, with tool configuration disabled. Model ID, access and region are still unverified.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents secret leakage into model prompts and logs.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Redact secrets before model input
requirementDrafts.statement: Secrets and credentials in logs/traces are redacted before any content is sent to the model.

requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Link conclusions to exact trace or log IDs
requirementDrafts.statement: Every conclusion cites exact trace or log IDs that exist in the retrieved evidence; uncited claims are rejected.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Blocks prompt injection from causing actions.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Prompt injection in a log cannot issue tool calls
requirementDrafts.statement: Log text is treated as untrusted data; the model has no tool-calling path and cannot trigger actions.

requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Missing spans yield uncertainty rather than invented causes
requirementDrafts.statement: When spans are missing, the answer states uncertainty and names the gap rather than inventing causes.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Retries and replays must not distort the incident timeline.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Repeated ingestion preserves a consistent incident timeline
requirementDrafts.statement: Re-ingesting the same events produces an identical incident timeline (deterministic event-ID keys, no duplicates).

request.message:
Act as a patient architecture consultant and teacher. Start with the exact evidence state. If blocked before checks, explicitly say runtime tests have not run and the design is not yet validated. An empty failures list NEVER means a sound, complete or correct design. Celebrate only named checks that actually passed. Explain the most important remaining issue in plain language and help the user make progress. Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Diagnose the first actionable finding. Propose a minimal supported architecture correction only when requirements already justify it; otherwise ask one precise question.
Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. Never clear unfinished-work gates, remove workload scope, weaken tests or invent successful validation. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. A local emulation pass is not a cloud plan or deployment. After an applied correction, rerun emulation on the new artifact; do not reuse this result. response.message:
No runtime checks have run yet, so this design is not validated at all. An empty failures list doesn't mean it passed. The run stopped at 8 blockers. Six are pipeline services (CloudWatch Logs, X-Ray, Firehose, the redaction Lambda, OpenSearch and the existing systems) that the generator can't build yet. That's product engineering work, not something we can fix by editing the diagram.

The first one we can fix ourselves is the Redacted archive (n-s3). Right now the diagram doesn't say who is allowed to read it, and that blocks the replay path that keeps the incident timeline consistent. Firehose writes to it, but no reader is named.

Which access should the existing Incident operator have to the archive? Read-only, so they can replay ingestion? Read and write? Or no direct access, with only the pipeline touching it? Once you choose, we'll add that one access link and rerun the emulation on the new export.
